newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips to cut jobs at Dutch LCD plant.
newsitem.headline: Philips to cut jobs at Dutch LCD plant.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Wednesday it would cut 190 jobs from a total of 540 at its liquid crystal display (LCD) production unit Flat Panel Displays (FDP) in the Dutch town of Eindhoven.
The company said in a statement the measure was necessary as the unit will next year start using a new production technology.
"Compulsory redundancies are unavoidable, but it is not yet known how many people will be affected," it added.
Philips said the transfer to the new production technology will be supported by its cooperation with Japan's Hosiden, which was announced last October.
The previously announced 50-50 joint venture with Hosiden will be called "Hosiden and Philips Display Cooperation" and will be sealed on March 31, 1997.
Philips said its flat panel displays sales activities in Europe and the U.S. would continue unchanged and that its research units will continue to support the development of active matrix LCDs.

The Dutch group said it considers LCD screens of great strategic importance and added the world-wide market for these displays is expected to trow to about $12 billion in the year 2001 from $4.6 billion in 1995.
"Philips FDP and Hosiden anticipate that their cooperation will allow them to realise a substantial increase in sales in this expanding market," Philips said.
LCD screens are used in notebook computers, desktop monitors, car navigation systems, test equipment, process automation and medical systems.
